title: Stata — xtset: Declare data to be panel data
use: Primary software-author explanation of within-panel calendar ordering, time steps, missing dates and panel balance. Chapter implements concepts with original standard-library Python.
verification: Retrieved official 15-page PDF; inspected within-panel lag interpretation, yearly/monthly gap examples and strongly/weakly balanced terminology, especially printed pages 5 and 8–10. No software installation or reproduction of vendor datasets. Chapter defines its own complete-date balance explicitly.

title: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis — How are personal consumption expenditures prices and quantities derived?
use: Method source for appropriate detailed price-index deflation and chain-weighted aggregation; original one-good example separately derives exact period-specific deflation.
verification: Retrieved official FAQ (page records modification 2026-10-02); inspected reference-year-100 detailed deflation and Fisher chain aggregation statements. No current PCE observations used and no claim that the synthetic example reproduces the complete official methodology.

title: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis — Why does BEA publish percent changes in quarterly series at annual rates?
use: Quarterly growth annualization through four-quarter compounding; distinguish growth-rate annualization from annualized flow-level units.
verification: Retrieved official FAQ and inspected quarterly-ratio and fourth-power formulas. Chapter uses original illustrative values rather than source historical GDP calculations or current releases.

title: Anna Mikusheva, MIT OpenCourseWare — Lecture Notes 1: Stationarity, Lag Operator, ARMA, and Covariance Structure
use: Further-study route for covariance stationarity, lag operators and moving-average covariance structure; chapter gives original finite-shock proofs and numerical laws.
verification: Retrieved official six-page PDF and inspected stationarity definitions, lag/MA constructions, random-walk variance and covariance structure. Internal notes cite Fall 2007 while OCW route/course metadata is Fall 2013; no unsupported edition/page claim beyond that inspected document. Infinite ARMA theory is identified as further study rather than assumed proved here.

title: Rob J Hyndman and George Athanasopoulos — Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed., Stationarity and differencing
use: Author-hosted further study connecting trends, seasonal differences and transformations to forecasting; original moment calculations establish the particular laws in this chapter.
verification: Retrieved chapter and inspected differencing/random-walk/drift/seasonal-difference discussion and caution about unnecessary differencing. Did not treat a rapidly decaying ACF as a universal condition of stationarity or a graph/test as proof; our common-random-component counterexample makes that limitation explicit. No source datasets or code copied.
